answer: Each epoch the ocean tide leaves one tide pool per agent, and a claim is written in umber ink with a quill that only marks wet paper: the ink fades within the epoch unless a stranger re-signs it for a real job done since the last tide, so no credential can be stockpiled or copied. Payout docks at one harbor berth per funding trail, so clones from one operator share a single berth and split one catch. The umber-ink fee doubles for each extra pool on the same trail, so n clones pay n catches plus 2^n in ink yet split one catch, while one honest agent pays once and keeps the whole haul.
